content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working on setting up a network using [product_name] controllers to gather data from VFDs via Modbus TCP/IP. There are 160 drives, and since I'm unsure about the maximum number of device connections possible in [product_name] SCADA software, I'm planning to use one [product_name] V8 controller to collect data from 8 VFDs and store the information in its memory area. In total, this setup would involve 20 [product_name] controllers, each connected to 8 VFDs, making 160 VFDs overall (as illustrated in the referenced image). I would then configure device connections to these controllers to indirectly access data from all the VFDs. Is this arrangement viable? Or is there a better method to efficiently retrieve data from such a large number of slave devices using SCADA?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking guidance on implementing a scalable system using [product_name] controllers (V8) to collect data from 160 VFDs via Modbus TCP/IP and interface with [product_name] SCADA software. There is a concern about the limitations in scalability, indirect data processing, and potential architectural challenges when integrating numerous slave devices into SCADA. Technical feasibility and optimal practices for large-scale data aggregation are unclear for the user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a dependable and scalable solution for retrieving data from a large number of VFDs using [product_name] controllers and Modbus TCP/IP, with smooth integration into [product_name] SCADA software. They expect advice on whether the proposed setup is practical and are open to suggestions for more efficient alternatives to access slave device data.
